subject: zeppelin
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: passenger zeppelin with gondola.
Style: art deco.
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module for an art deco passenger zeppelin with a gondola, considering plain object props with a few jointed parts like propellers and fins, and working through how the floating vehicle should be positioned since it's airborne rather than resting on the ground.

I decide to go with a landed-ish pose: lower fin tip and gondola wheel/bumper both resting at y≈0, similar to how the Hindenburg had support wheels, which should read well visually. I also note the real-world scale issue — passenger zeppelins are over 200m long, which is huge for a model viewer unless the pitch specifies otherwise.

I settle on a more moderate stylized size of about 90m length and 18m diameter (radius 9), reasoning that decoration should come from textures rather than paint resolution given the scale. For layout, I decide the airship faces +Z with nose at +Z, built as a lofted hull sweep from tail to nose using a 16-sided low-poly cross-section.

I work out vertical placement so the lower fin and gondola wheel both touch the ground plane: setting the hull center height around y≈13 so the gondola (hanging below the hull front) and tail fin extension reach down to y=0. For the art deco styling, I settle on a champagne/cream hull with deep teal/navy bands, gold trim, sunburst motifs, and a chevron strip.

I also plan out the decorative details: a sunburst emblem decal on the nose, an "AURORA" nameplate in art deco lettering, window-strip texture on the gondola, fin chevron patterns, and riveted panels, with brass metal trim and gold stripes running along the hull at specific angular bands, plus navy coloring on the belly. I'm aiming for a part count between 180-340, starting to list out components: the hull sweep mesh, nose and tail cone caps, and fins.

Now I'm detailing the fins with edge trim rods and separate hinged rudder/elevator flaps, the gondola body with window textures, railings, and four propeller nacelles with spinning joints, plus longitudinal hull ribs and frame rings — considering whether to build the rings as swept loops or torus geometry.

For rings I'll use torus geometry at each station, sized by the hull's radius function for an exact fit. Beyond that I'm planning decals (sunburst, nameplate, flags), a mooring nose cone, belly window strips, gondola details like searchlights and antenna wires, running-light glows, and the four engine cars each with cylinder bodies, props, and strut rods to the hull.

Now I'm setting up the actual build with constants for length, radius, and vertical offset, then defining the hull path and radius function before writing the geometry code.

Refining the radius profile to avoid a pointy tail, clamping the minimum radius so the tail has a small flat end instead of tapering to zero, while the nose gets a rounded cap extending beyond the body length.

For the hull coloring, I'm setting up a paint function keyed on sweep position and angle around the circumference — cream base with warm top and cool belly shading, gold stripe bands at specific angle ranges, a navy underside, and subtle panel seam texture via noise, keeping the overall palette restrained.

Since cap vertices sit exactly at t=1, I can use that to gold-tint the nose dome and navy-tint the tail cap distinctly from the hull body. I'm also planning longitudinal gold rib rods swept along several angles down the fuselage for added detail.

Now for frame rings, I'm placing torus geometry at several stations along the length, needing to reorient the torus's axis to align with the fuselage's z-direction since it defaults to lying flat in xy.

For the skeleton, I decide I don't strictly need joints for a static model, but I'll add a root hull joint plus prop and rudder hinge joints anyway. Since unparented geometry snaps to the nearest bone and could accidentally attach to a prop joint instead of hull, I need to explicitly assign the hull bone to every hull-adjacent part to avoid misattachment.

Now I'm working out the tail fin geometry—four cruciform fins positioned along the tail taper, defining their side-view outlines relative to the hull axis so the fin roots sink properly into the hull surface.

Computing the hull radius at a couple more sample points along the taper, then laying out the fin root profile with a stepped art-deco leading edge made from a few angular cut points near the tip.

I'm also sketching a separate movable rudder flap at the trailing tail edge, with its own small outline and a hinge joint connecting it to the fin root.

For the four stabilizer fins, I'm defining the extrusion directions (up, down, left, right) and figuring out the perpendicular axes so thickness extrudes correctly for each orientation.

For the fin coloring, I'm setting a cream base with navy chevron-style stripe bands computed from a modulo pattern on local coordinates, plus a navy band near the tip edge.

Now I'm adding an art deco sunburst motif on the fins, computing ray angles from a root point so the bands fan out radially. For the gondola, I'm calculating the hull's radius at different depths to position it tucked under the hull belly between z=8 and z=26.

I'm lofting the gondola body through several cross-section stations, tapering from a narrow nose to a wider box midsection and back, using a box-shaped section for the envelope sweep.

For the windows, I'm planning to add textured strip planes on the side and front faces—dark navy with gold-framed, warm-lit window cutouts rendered via SVG—positioned to wrap around the narrower front face.

Now I'm adding gondola trim: gold rods along bottom and top edges plus a keel, a bumper wheel cylinder with strut, a small glowing searchlight under the front, and a gold crest for the gondola's nameplate. Then I'm positioning four engine cars symmetrically along the hull, calculating their x-offset from the hull radius at each z-position.

For the engine cars themselves, I'm giving each a capsule-shaped body with a rear-mounted propeller (hub plus blades) attached via a joint parented to the hull, plus struts connecting the car to the hull surface -- computing the rod endpoints by projecting toward the hull center so the inner ends stay hidden inside the hull.

Propeller blades use thin boxes oriented perpendicular to the prop axis, with one blade pointing up and a second rotated 90° to form a four-blade cross shape at the hub.

Now I'm thinking about adding a long passenger window strip along the lower hull belly, Hindenburg-style.

For the hull windows, I'm placing a decal on both sides of the hull surface at the lower flank angle, using the surface normal as direction with a wide, thin size to create a horizontal window band, then planning a sunburst emblem decal near the nose on each flank.

A nameplate decal spelling "AURORA" goes near mid-length, and I'm deciding to skip decals on the tail fins in favor of plain paint. For the nose, I'm adding a gold mooring cone spike at the tip, and considering whether to add nose rings or a sunburst detail there too.

For the sunburst, I'm computing 16 gold rods radiating outward from the nose tip across the dome surface, calculating each rod's direction using an elevation angle and azimuthal spread around the dome center, as an alternative to a simple painted stripe.

Now I'm planning the tail cap with a glowing white tail light, plus port/starboard running lights (red on the left, green on the right) as small glowing spheres along the hull sides. I'm also sketching thin rigging wires connecting the fin tips to the hull, plus considering a decal emblem on the upper fin surface.

Now I'm writing the paint function for the hull, applying gold to the nose dome and defining shading rules based on surface position and normal direction for a warm-top, cool-bottom lighting effect...

Working out texel density...I'll use a 2048 paint size with thin seams so they stay subtle, and add fine noise to the cream color for a fabric feel, plus a soft lighting falloff and a defined color palette for cream, navy, and teal.

Now I'm planning the texture set: lit gondola and promenade windows with glow, a gold sunburst emblem on navy, a deco "AURORA" nameplate, a fin crest, and a reused smaller gondola emblem — keeping everything within the flat color budget.

I'm also sketching out the joint structure for the propellers and rudder, defining roles like "fan" and "hinge," and figuring out how the rudder's extrude origin should align with the tail root coordinates relative to the hinge joint position.

Then I'm setting up glow spheres for the lights and writing a hull radius function to compute ring sizes at specific stations along the fuselage.

For the window decal placement, I'm mapping ring stations to z-coordinates and figuring out the clock angles so the promenade windows sit diagonally, about 30° below horizontal on each side, with symmetric placement left and right.

Now I'm placing the sunburst emblem and nameplate decals with their positions, angles, and sizes. I'm also reasoning through whether text decals need mirroring on the opposite side—concluding they don't, since the drawing projects toward the viewer and reads correctly as drawn, unlike the toon eye asymmetry case which actually needs the mirror flag.

Working out the fin decal placement and projection direction, then shaping the fin's outline points to define its planform, tapering from the root toward the trailing edge where the rudder sits.

Finishing the rudder geometry with a hinge along the trailing edge, keeping all vertices sharp and giving it some thickness. I'm also calculating hull radius at different z positions to figure out where the fin root sits relative to the hull surface, then sketching a sunburst ray pattern radiating from the fin's root-trailing corner for the paint scheme.

Instead of trying to match gold trim precisely to the fin outline, I'll simplify by adding gold arc bands at two radii and placing gold trim rods along the fin's edge segments directly — six edges per fin across four fins gives a clean 24-rod trim solution.

Now I'm turning to the engine cars, modeling them as capsules positioned fore-aft along the hull with gold cowl rings and props, then connecting them to the hull with angled gold struts computed from the hull's surface normal at each car's position. I'm also planning the gondola's side window strips as thin planes along its sides.

I'm also figuring out how the gondola's box-section loft should taper between its stations, keeping the window strip planes constrained within the straight mid-section so they don't poke through the curved transition zones.

Simpler plan: build the gondola from plain boxes instead—a main rectangular box for the body, plus a tapered frustum box at the front and rear, giving a crisp blocky shape rather than relying on the catmull-interpolated loft.

I'm figuring out the paint scheme: navy for the lower body, cream for the upper band, with gold trim rods along the edges and roofline. Still working out window strip placement on the side and front faces.

For the gondola, I'm adding a bumper wheel cylinder with a strut connecting it to the gondola bottom, and considering a small skid near the lower fin tip, though the fin already reaches the ground cleanly. I'm skipping the catwalk ladder but adding an antenna mast near the nose with a glow light and connecting wires to the upper fin tip.

I'm computing the hull radius at the mast position to get the top y-coordinate, then running wires from the mast to the upper fin tip and forward to the nose dome, plus adding cruciform bracing wires between the fin tips for extra structural detail.

Now I'm working out the gilt sunburst rods radiating from the nose dome center, placing tip points on the sphere surface and connecting rods between them, while checking that the chords don't dip too far inside the dome's radius.

Adding the tail cap with a glowing light sphere, then setting up decal placement helpers and a shared gilt metal paint. I'm layering in glowing window decals, a forward-facing gold searchlight under the gondola, and red/green running lights on either side.

Now I'm checking the hull sweep's path and radius configuration, making sure ring density adapts where the radius changes, and considering how roll orientation behaves along the +z path direction.

For `hull.line`, I'm figuring the path should trace along the surface at a given clock angle with knots at bone cuts, sliced to [0.1, 0.95]. I'm also verifying the torus rings placed along the hull account for circumscribed polygon geometry—since flat faces sit at radius r, vertices extend outward by about 1.25%, so I need the torus tube thickness to clear that offset without poking through.

For the ribs, I'm placing them every 36° to land on face centers of the 20-sided hull, giving 10 ribs total, each with a small radius and slight lift. Then I'm working out the window decals' angular positions, snapping them to the nearest face centers around 126° and 234°.

I'm positioning the nameplate at 90°/270° and checking it fits between neighboring ribs without touching them, then checking the sunburst decal's angular span near the nose for possible overlap with the nearby ribs at 72° and 108°—finding it's a near miss, slightly tight but roughly acceptable.

Now I'm sizing the window decal and checking its clearance from the ribs at 216°/252°, which looks fine. I'm then sketching the nameplate SVG with gold art-deco "AURORA" lettering in a bold sans-serif with wide letter-spacing and flanking lines, and starting the sunburst SVG with a navy circle and gold triangular rays.

Now I'm designing the fin crest as a deco fan motif with sunburst rays over a stepped base, then building the gondola window strip as a dark frame with twelve gold-mullioned window rects.

Scaling up the hull windows to eighteen across, I'm making sure the gondola's color tint varies by vertical position and that the lower fin tip and gondola wheel both sit flush at y=0. Now I'm defining the fin's trim rod edges by tracing the outline points into a connected sequence of gold rods along the fin's profile.

I need to drop the trailing edge segment since that's where the rudder hinges, so only edges 1 through 5 become rods, and I'm computing their positions using the fin's local coordinate space. Checking the taper, I realize rods near the root are getting buried since the fin's thickness there is much larger than the rod radius, so I'm adjusting the thickness taper from 0.5 down to 0.15 to keep the rods visible along the span.

I'm giving the rudder its own thinner taper profile, and now I need to decide what to do with the deterministic `rng` import -- since unused imports might trigger a typecheck error, I'll actually put it to use by jittering torus ring tube radii slightly for subtle variation. Now I'm starting the fin's paint function.

Writing fin shader logic...

Still writing hull paint logic...

For the engine car I'll use a simpler shading rule based on normal direction instead of reusing the hull paint. I still need to export the meta, add a sunburst decal on the hull aligned to a surface point, and set up the rings as a torus with its axis along z for proper placement.

For the propeller, I'm placing the joint at the hub with direction pointing backward, but I'm running into trouble orienting the blade boxes correctly -- the axis mapping is putting the blade's thin edge vertical instead of making the blade plane perpendicular to the prop axis like it should be. I need to fix the direction/orientation parameters so the blade actually faces the right way.

Fixing blade orientation and material...

I realize the blade would clip into the hull at the given car position, so I need to push the car further out—placing it at roughly hullRadius+3.4 so the 2.6-unit blade tip clears the hull with a safety margin, then double-checking the actual distance from the hull center meets that threshold. I'm also setting the strut target to point from the hull center outward to just inside the hull radius, and sketching the hub/prop placement relative to the car's capsule body.

Now I'm laying out the gondola's trim rods along the bottom and top edges plus corner posts, adding a gold keel strip, and noting that the catwalk connecting gondola to hull should sit flush since their heights nearly match. I'm also tallying up the part counts across the hull, ribs, rings, nose assembly, fins, rudders, connecting rods, wires, and gondola pieces to get a sense of total model complexity.

Tallying up engines, decals, and mast pieces brings the total part count to roughly 140, a bit under my 180 target, so I'm considering adding gold medallion-style discs along the hull's waist stripe to fill it out further.

Placing 28 small deco medallions along the teal belly band at carefully chosen angles so they sit flush on the surface, then adding three gold speed-line fins on each side of the gondola near the rear for an art deco touch. I'm also considering hull registration lettering as a decal.

For functional details, I'm setting window glow strength, confirming stick/frame parts use the gilt paint color, adding red/green mast lights and a promenade glow decal, and naming the rudder hinges and propeller fans with proper roles. Now writing the fin generation loop...

Still writing fin and rudder geometry...

I'm placing the decal only on the top fin near the surface, then checking I've got all the needed imports (bezier, rgb, noise, mix, smoothstep, paint) and confirming the hinge/joint role option and decal bone option are valid. I'm also drafting the SVG text styling for the "AURORA" wordmark with a condensed sans-serif font stack and wide letter spacing, then moving on to build the window strip SVG.

Now I'm designing the sunburst SVG with concentric navy/gold circles and radiating gold rays, plus a crest SVG with a fan of rays over a semicircle and bars underneath, and starting to think through how glow intensity should vary by part.

I'm double-checking the capsule geometry helper for tapered radius bars with rounded caps, confirming torus coloring uses the gilt paint, and verifying the hull positioning function against the dorsal clock reference before finalizing everything.
